Use Rails in API-only mode; the frontend is a separate app.

Use `DATABASE_URL`. Work in `/app`.

  "output_head": "# Helpdesk API

Rails API-only backend for a helpdesk SaaS. Businesses sign up, their owners verify
email and sign in, and each business has its own users. The frontend is a separate
app that talks to this API over JSON under `/api/v1`.

## Setup

Requires Ruby 4.0, PostgreSQL and the gems in the `Gemfile`.

```sh
bundle install
export DATABASE_URL=postgresql:///helpdesk_development?host=/var/lib/postgresql
bin/rails db:prepare                 # creates and migrates the development database
RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails db:prepare  # the test database (a "_test" sibling of DATABASE_URL)
bin/rails server                     # listens on PORT (default 3000)
bin/rails test                       # the suite never touches the development database
```

Outgoing mail is written to `tmp/mails/` in development.

### Environment variables

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | none (required) | PostgreSQL connection. |
| `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | `DATABASE_URL` with `_development` replaced by `_test` | Test database. Tests never use the development database. |
| `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL` | `http://localhost:3001` | Frontend base URL. Used for email links and as the only allowed CORS origin. |
| `HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM` | `support@example.test` | Sender address for all mail. |
| `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_DOMAIN`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD` | `localhost`, `587`, — | Production mail delivery. |

## Conventions

- Every request body uses an envelope, e.g. `{"session": {...}}`. Bare JSON is rejected.
- **Choosing a business:** send `X-Helpdesk-Account: <subdomain>`.
  - Signed-in requests can omit it. The token already identifies the business. If it is sent and does not match, the response is 403.
  - Sign-in, verification resend and password reset use it to find the user. Without it, the email must belong to exactly one business.
- **Signed-in requests:** send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
- **Lists** take `page` (default 1) and `per_page` (default 25, at most 100). They return the records under the plural resource name (`requests`, `tickets`, `comments`), plus `count` (all matches, not just this page), `page`, `per_page`, `next_page` and `previous_page`. The last two are `null` when there is no such page.
- **Errors** share one shape: `{"error": {"code": "...", "message": "...", "errors": {...}}}`. `errors` is present for validation failures. Validation keys are prefixed `account.` or `admin.` on signup, and `comment.` on ticket replies.
- Timestamps are ISO 8601 UTC.

## Endpoints

| Method and path | Auth | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `POST /api/v1/registrations` | header required | Customer signs up for the business's portal, `{"user": {"name", "email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `user` (role `customer`). The user is unverified and gets a verification email. Then the usual verification, sign-in, profile and password-reset flows apply. An email with a pending invitation is refused with `422`, as if it were taken. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/create` | none | Sign up a business and its admin. Returns `201` with `account` and `user`. The admin is unverified and receives a verification email. |
| `GET /api/v1/portal` | header | Public `{"portal": {"name", "subdomain"}}`. |
| `POST /api/v1/sessions` | header optional | Sign in with `{"session": {"email", "password"}}`. Returns `201` with `session.token`, `user` and `account`. Unverified users get `403 email_not_verified`. Suspended users get `403 user_suspended`. |
| `DELETE /api/v1/session` | bearer | Sign out this session. `204`. |
| `GET /api/v1/me` / `PATCH /api/v1/me` | bearer | Profile. `PATCH` takes `{"user": {"name": "..."}}`. |
| `PUT /api/v1/me/password` | bearer | `{"password_change": {"current_password", "password"}}`. Signs out every session, including this one. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202`. |
| `POST /api/v1/email_verifications/confirm` | header optional | `{"email_verification": {"token"}}`. Marks the user verified. The token works once. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"email"}}`. Sends a new link and replaces the old one. Returns `202` whether or not the email exists. |
| `POST /api/v1/password_resets/confirm` | header optional | `{"password_reset": {"token", "password"}}`. Sets the password, signs out all sessions and verifies the email. The token works once. |
| `GET /api/v1/account` | bearer | Full account, including `status` and `reactivation_deadline`. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/cancel` | bearer, owner | Cancels the business and revokes all its sessions. |
| `POST /api/v1/account/reactivate` | bearer, owner | Reactivates a cancelled business within 90 days. |
| `GET /api/v1/requests` | bearer | The signed-in user's own requests, most recently active first, under `requests`. Filter with `?status=` set to `open`, `pending` or `solved`. |

- **Assignment**: `assignee_id` names a staff member who is active (an admin or agent, not suspended) in the same business. Anything else is refused with `422` on `assignee_id`, and nothing in that update is saved. Customers cannot assign requests.
- **Priority** is `normal` or `high`, and a new request is `normal`. Staff set it with `priority` on a reply, alone or with the rest. `null` and anything else are refused with `422` on `priority`, and nothing in that update is saved. Priority is internal: it appears in staff `ticket` responses only, never in a customer's `request`. A customer's `priority` is ignored, so a reply with only a `priority` is a bad request, as with `assignee_id`.

### Filtering

- `GET /tickets` filters by `status`, `priority`, `requester_id`, `assignee_id` and `q`. The filters combine, so a request must match every one that is sent, for example `GET /tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt`.
- `requester_id` and `assignee_id` take a user ID. `assignee_id=unassigned` means nobody is assigned. An unknown user ID matches nothing.
- `q` is a case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched. The text is literal: `%`, `_` and `\` match only themselves. A blank `q` is no search.
- `GET /requests` filters a customer's own requests by `status` only. Other filters, `priority` included, are for staff and are ignored there.
- A blank filter value means no filter. A value that is not allowed is refused with `422`, naming the parameter, as in `{"error": {"code": "validation_failed", ..."errors": {"status": ["must be one of open, pending, solved"]}}}`.

## Invitations

Admins add people by inviting them. Only `admin` and `agent` can be invited. Customers register through the portal instead.

- `POST /invitations` emails a link to `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/accept-invitation?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`. The API never returns the token, and stores only its digest.
- An email can have **one pending invitation per business**, whatever the role. A second one is refused with `422`. Resend the first one instead. An email that already belongs to someone in the business cannot be invited either.
- Invitations are **pending**, **accepted**, **revoked** or **expired**. Expiry comes from the clock, so an expired invitation needs no job. An expired invitation no longer blocks a fresh one for the same email.
- Accepted and revoked invitations can no longer be resent or revoked, with `422 invitation_closed`. Resending a pending or expired invitation issues a new token and restarts the 7-day clock.
- Accepting creates the user with the invited email and role, already verified. The new person signs in straight away, with no further email.
- Customer registration refuses an email that has a pending invitation, reporting it as taken. The portal does not reveal who has been invited.
- Accepting refuses a business that has been cancelled, with `403 account_cancelled`.

## Suspension

- An admin suspends or reinstates anyone in the business with `PATCH /users/:id`.
- Suspending signs the person out of every session, clears the tickets they were assigned, and stops them signing in (`403 user_suspended`). Reinstating does not bring back their old sessions, so they sign in again.
- The last active admin cannot be suspended, not even by themselves. This is checked under the business lock, so two admins cannot suspend each other at the same moment.
- Suspended people are not offered as assignees, and are left out of `GET /staff`.

## Concurrency

Creating and resending invitations, accepting them, customer registration, suspension, and any change of assignee each run under the business's row lock. That keeps the rules above (one pending invitation per email, no registration over an invitation, at least one active admin, and no suspended assignee) true under concurrent requests.

## Layout

- `app/models/account.rb`: business, cancellation, reactivation window, purge.
- `app/models/user.rb`: users, roles, password rules.
- `app/models/session.rb`: bearer sessions (only token digests are stored).
- `app/models/ticket.rb`: requests, their status rules and assignment. `app/models/comment.rb`: the conversation, with private notes.
- `app/models/invitation.rb`: invitations, their statuses, acceptance and the one-pending-per-email rule.
- `app/models/concerns/single_use_token.rb`: replaceable, single-use tokens for verification and reset.
- `app/controllers/concerns/`: error format, business lookup from header, bearer auth and cancelled-account rules, pagination, list filters, reply parsing, and strict true/false parsing.
- `app/controllers/api/v1/`: endpoints.
- `app/mailers/user_mailer.rb`: verification, reset and invitation emails.
- `config/initializers/helpdesk.rb`: settings from the environment. `config/initializers/cors.rb`: frontend CORS.

ts place in the lists and the customer sees nothing new. A status sent with them still applies, as it always does.
- **Assignment**: `assignee_id` names a staff member who is active (an admin or agent, not suspended) in the same business. Anything else is refused with `422` on `assignee_id`, and nothing in that update is saved. Customers cannot assign requests.
- **Priority** is `normal` or `high`, and a new request is `normal`. Staff set it with `priority` on a reply, alone or with the rest. `null` and anything else are refused with `422` on `priority`, and nothing in that update is saved. Priority is internal: it appears in staff `ticket` responses only, never in a customer's `request`. A customer's `priority` is ignored, so a reply with only a `priority` is a bad request, as with `assignee_id`.

### Filtering

- `GET /tickets` filters by `status`, `priority`, `requester_id`, `assignee_id` and `q`. The filters combine, so a request must match every one that is sent, for example `GET /tickets?status=open&assignee_id=unassigned&priority=high&q=receipt`.
- `requester_id` and `assignee_id` take a user ID. `assignee_id=unassigned` means nobody is assigned. An unknown user ID matches nothing.
- `q` is a case-insensitive search through subjects and public comments. Private notes are not searched. The text is literal: `%`, `_` and `\` match only themselves. A blank `q` is no search.
- `GET /requests` filters a customer's own requests by `status` only. Other filters, `priority` included, are for staff and are ignored there.
- A blank filter value means no filter. A value that is not allowed is refused with `422`, naming the parameter, as in `{"error": {"code": "validation_failed", ..."errors": {"status": ["must be one of open, pending, solved"]}}}`.

## Invitations

Admins add people by inviting them. Only `admin` and `agent` can be invited. Customers register through the portal instead.

- `POST /invitations` emails a link to `HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL/accept-invitation?account=<subdomain>&token=<token>`. The API never returns the token, and stores only its digest.
- An email can have **one pending invitation per business**, whatever the role. A second one is refused with `422`. Resend the first one instead. An email that already belongs to someone in the business cannot be invited either.
- Invitations are **pending**, **accepted**, **revoked** or **expired**. Expiry comes from the clock, so an expired invitation needs no job. An expired invitation no longer blocks a fresh one for the same email.
- Accepted and revoked invitations can no longer be resent or revoked, with `422 invitation_closed`. Resending a pending or expired invitation issues a new token and restarts the 7-day clock.
- Accepting creates the user with the invited email and role, already verified. The new person signs in straight away, with no further email.
- Customer registration refuses an email that has a pending invitation, reporting it as taken. The portal does not reveal who has been invited.
- Accepting refuses a business that has been cancelled, with `403 account_cancelled`.

## Suspension

- An admin suspends or reinstates anyone in the business with `PATCH /users/:id`.
- Suspending signs the person out of every session, clears the tickets they were assigned, and stops them signing in (`403 user_suspended`). Reinstating does not bring back their old sessions, so they sign in again.
- The last active admin cannot be suspended, not even by themselves. This is checked under the business lock, so two admins cannot suspend each other at the same moment.
- Suspended people are not offered as assignees, and are left out of `GET /staff`.

## Concurrency

Creating and resending invitations, accepting them, customer registration, suspension, and any change of assignee each run under the business's row lock. That keeps the rules above (one pending invitation per email, no registration over an invitation, at least one active admin, and no suspended assignee) true under concurrent requests.

## Layout

- `app/models/account.rb`: business, cancellation, reactivation window, purge.
- `app/models/user.rb`: users, roles, password rules.
- `app/models/session.rb`: bearer sessions (only token digests are stored).
- `app/models/ticket.rb`: requests, their status rules and assignment. `app/models/comment.rb`: the conversation, with private notes.
- `app/models/invitation.rb`: invitations, their statuses, acceptance and the one-pending-per-email rule.
- `app/models/concerns/single_use_token.rb`: replaceable, single-use tokens for verification and reset.
- `app/controllers/concerns/`: error format, business lookup from header, bearer auth and cancelled-account rules, pagination, list filters, reply parsing, and strict true/false parsing.
- `app/controllers/api/v1/`: endpoints.
- `app/mailers/user_mailer.rb`: verification, reset and invitation emails.
- `config/initializers/helpdesk.rb`: settings from the environment. `config/initializers/cors.rb`: frontend CORS.

- The signing-up user is an `admin` and acts as the business owner. Only admins can cancel or reactivate.

- Subdomains are unique across all businesses and must not be reserved (`www`, `api`, `app`, `admin`, ...).

### Cancellation

- `POST /account/cancel` sets `cancelled_at` and revokes every session in the business.
- While cancelled, only the owner can sign in. Ordinary access returns `403 account_cancelled`. The owner can still view the account, edit their profile, change their password, sign out, and reactivate.
- `POST /account/reactivate` works until 90 days after cancellation.
- Data is kept until the reactivation window closes.

### Permanent deletion

```sh
bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
```

This deletes every account cancelled more than 90 days ago, along with its users, sessions, tokens, requests and comments. Run it on a schedule, for example daily from cron. It is safe to run repeatedly.

## Requests

A request is one record with a subject, a status and a conversation. Customers see it at `/requests`, and staff at `/tickets`. Both views are the same records.

- A new request is `open`. Opening one needs a `subject` and a first `comment.body`. Both are saved, or neither is.
- Statuses are `open`, `pending` and `solved`.
- **Customer replies** can carry a comment, a status, or both. A status can only be `solved`, so `pending` or `open` is refused with `422`. A comment reopens a `pending` or `solved` request, unless the same update marks it `solved`.
- **Staff replies** can carry a comment, a status, an assignee, or a combination. Any of the three statuses is allowed. A reply without a status leaves the status alone, so a staff reply never reopens a request by itself.
- A reply with a comment and a status is applied as one update. If either part is invalid, nothing is saved.
- **Private notes**: staff can send `comment: {body, public: false}`. Only staff see them. A customer's comment is always public, so `public` is ignored for them. Anything other than `true` or `false` for `public` is refused with `422`, so a typo cannot post a note publicly. Customers see only public comments on their own requests. Staff see every comment.
- Comment bodies are limited to 10,000 characters. Subjects are limited to 255.
- Replies send no email. The conversation is only in the portal.
- Activity moves a request up the lists: opening, replying with a public comment, or changing its status. Comments are listed oldest first.
- **Internal activity leaves the customer's view unchanged.** A private note, an assignment or a priority change sent on its own does not change the request's `status` or `updated_at`, so the request keeps its place in the lists and the customer sees nothing new. A status sent with them still applies, as it always does.
- **Assignment**: `assignee_id` names a staff member who is active (an admin or agent, not suspended) in the same business. Anything else is refused with `422` on `assignee_id`, and nothing in that update is saved. Customers cannot assign requests.
- **Priority** is `normal` or `high`, and a new request is `normal`. Staff set it with `priority` on a reply, alone or with the rest. `null` and anything else are refused with `422` on `priority`, and nothing in that update is saved. Priority is internal: it appears in staff `ticket` responses only, never in a customer's `request`. A customer's `priority` is ignored, so a reply with only a `priority` is a bad request, as with `assignee_id`.

- Email addresses are unique within a business, so one email can belong to several businesses.
- Subdomains are unique across all businesses and must not be reserved (`www`, `api`, `app`, `admin`, ...).

### Cancellation

- `POST /account/cancel` sets `cancelled_at` and revokes every session in the business.
- While cancelled, only the owner can sign in. Ordinary access returns `403 account_cancelled`. The owner can still view the account, edit their profile, change their password, sign out, and reactivate.
- `POST /account/reactivate` works until 90 days after cancellation.
- Data is kept until the reactivation window closes.

### Permanent deletion

```sh
bin/rails helpdesk:purge_cancelled_accounts
```

This deletes every account cancelled more than 90 days ago, along with its users, sessions, tokens, requests and comments. Run it on a schedule, for example daily from cron. It is safe to run repeatedly.

## Requests

A request is one record with a subject, a status and a conversation. Customers see it at `/requests`, and staff at `/tickets`. Both views are the same records.

- A new request is `open`. Opening one needs a `subject` and a first `comment.body`. Both are saved, or neither is.
- Statuses are `open`, `pending` and `solved`.
- **Customer replies** can carry a comment, a status, or both. A status can only be `solved`, so `pending` or `open` is refused with `422`. A comment reopens a `pending` or `solved` request, unless the same update marks it `solved`.
- **Staff replies** can carry a comment, a status, an assignee, or a combination. Any of the three statuses is allowed. A reply without a status leaves the status alone, so a staff reply never reopens a request by itself.
- A reply with a comment and a status is applied as one update. If either part is invalid, nothing is saved.
- **Private notes**: staff can send `comment: {body, public: false}`. Only staff see them. A customer's comment is always public, so `public` is ignored for them. Anything other than `true` or `false` for `public` is refused with `422`, so a typo cannot post a note publicly. Customers see only public comments on their own requests. Staff see every comment.
- Comment bodies are limited to 10,000 characters. Subjects are limited to 255.
- Replies send no email. The conversation is only in the portal.
- Activity moves a request up the lists: opening, replying with a public comment, or changing its status. Comments are listed oldest first.
- **Internal activity leaves the customer's view unchanged.** A private note, an assignment or a priority change sent on its own does not change the request's `status` or `updated_at`, so the request keeps its place in the lists and the customer sees nothing new. A status sent with them still applies, as it always does.
- **Assignment**: `assignee_id` names a staff member who is active (an admin or agent, not suspended) in the same business. Anything else is refused with `422` on `assignee_id`, and nothing in that update is saved. Customers cannot assign requests.
- **Priority** is `normal` or `high`, and a new request is `normal`. Staff set it with `priority` on a reply, alone or with the rest. `null` and anything else are refused with `422` on `priority`, and nothing in that update is saved. Priority is internal: it appears in staff `ticket` responses only, never in a customer's `request`. A customer's `priority` is ignored, so a reply with only a `priority` is a bad request, as with `assignee_id`.

module Helpdesk
  # Runtime settings, read from the environment when used so that changing the
  # environment (for example in tests) takes effect without restarting.
  module Settings
    DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL = "http://localhost:3001".freeze
    DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM = "support@example.test".freeze

    class << self
      # Base URL of the separately hosted frontend, without a trailing slash.
      def frontend_url
        (ENV["HELPDESK_FRONTEND_URL"].presence || DEFAULT_FRONTEND_URL).delete_suffix("/")
      end

      # Scheme, host and port only. This is the value browsers send as the Origin header.
      def frontend_origin
        uri = URI.parse(frontend_url)
        port = uri.port == uri.default_port ? "" : ":#{uri.port}"
        "#{uri.scheme}://#{uri.host}#{port}"
      end

      # Link the frontend turns into a request, e.g. /verify-email?account=acme&token=...
      def frontend_link(path, account:, token:)
        "#{frontend_url}#{path}?#{{ account: account, token: token }.to_query}"
      end

      def mail_from
        ENV["HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM"].presence || DEFAULT_MAIL_FROM
      end
    end
  end

# Chooses the business for a request from the X-Helpdesk-Account header.
module AccountScoped
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  ACCOUNT_HEADER = "X-Helpdesk-Account".freeze

  private

  def requested_subdomain
    request.headers[ACCOUNT_HEADER].to_s.strip.downcase.presence
  end

  # The business named by the header, or nil if no header was sent. If the
  # header names an unknown business, this renders 404 and the caller must stop
  # (check `performed?`).
  def optional_account_from_header
    return nil if requested_subdomain.nil?

    account = Account.find_by(subdomain: requested_subdomain)
    render_error(:not_found, "account_not_found", "No business matches the X-Helpdesk-Account header.") unless account
    account
  end

  # Like optional_account_from_header, but the header is required. Renders 400
  # when it is missing.
  def account_from_header!
    if requested_subdomain.nil?
      render_error(:bad_request, "account_header_required", "Send the X-Helpdesk-Account header to choose a business.")
      return nil
    end

    optional_account_from_header

# Bearer-token sessions. Callers include `before_action :authenticate_session!`.
#
# A cancelled account blocks everything except the actions listed with
# `available_while_cancelled`, which the owner needs to reactivate the account.
module Authenticatable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  included do
    class_attribute :cancelled_account_actions, instance_writer: false, default: [].freeze
  end

  class_methods do
    def available_while_cancelled(*actions)
      self.cancelled_account_actions = (cancelled_account_actions + actions.map(&:to_s)).freeze
    end
  end

  private

  attr_reader :current_session, :current_user, :current_account

  def authenticate_session!
    session = Session.find_active(bearer_token)
    return render_error(:unauthorized, "unauthenticated", "Sign in to continue.") unless session

    user = session.user
    account = user.account

    # Suspending a user deletes their sessions, so this only guards against a session that outlived the suspension.
    return render_error(:unauthorized, "unauthenticated", "Sign in to continue.") if user.suspended?

    if requested_subdomain && requested_subdomain != account.subdomain
      return render_error(:forbidden, "account_mismatch", "This session belongs to a different business.")
    end

    @current_session = session
    @current_user = user
    @current_account = account

    return if !account.cancelled? || self.class.cancelled_account_actions.include?(action_name)

    render_error(:forbidden, "account_cancelled", "This business has been cancelled.")
  end

  def require_account_owner!
    return if current_user.admin?

    render_error(:forbidden, "owner_only", "Only the account owner can do that.")
  end

  # Admins manage people and invitations. Agents and customers cannot.
  def require_admin!
    return if current_user.admin?

    render_error(:forbidden, "admin_only", "Only admins can do that.")
  end

  # Staff (admins and agents) work the helpdesk. Customers only see their own requests.
  def require_staff!
    return if current_user.staff?

    render_error(:forbidden, "staff_only", "Only business staff can do that.")
  end

  def bearer_token
    request.authorization.to_s[/\ABearer\s+(\S+)\z/i, 1]
  end
end

  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

# Reads the filters on a list. Each filter is optional, and a blank value means no filter. A value that is not
# allowed adds an error under the parameter's name, so the caller can answer 422 instead of guessing.
module ListFilters
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # A user ID as the database stores it: digits only, within the bigint range.
  USER_ID_FORMAT = /\A\d{1,18}\z/

  private

  # One of +allowed+, or nil when the parameter is absent or blank.
  def choice_param(name, allowed, errors)
    value = params[name].to_s.strip
    return nil if value.empty?
    return value if allowed.include?(value)

    errors[name] = [ "must be one of #{allowed.join(", ")}" ]
    nil
  end

  # A user ID, or a word from +also+ returned as given, or nil when absent or blank.
  def user_id_param(name, errors, also: [])
    value = params[name].to_s.strip
    return nil if value.empty?
    return value if also.include?(value)
    return value.to_i if value.match?(USER_ID_FORMAT)

    errors[name] = [ "must be #{[ "a user ID", *also ].join(" or ")}" ]
    nil
  end

  # The search text exactly as typed, or nil when absent or blank. It is not trimmed, so the text the user types
  # is the text that is matched. Anything other than text is an error.
  def text_param(name, errors)
    value = params[name]
    return nil if value.blank?
    return value if value.is_a?(String) && !value.include?("\u0000")

    errors[name] = [ "must be text" ]
    nil
  end
end

# Offset pagination for list endpoints, using ?page= and ?per_page= (defaults 1 and 25).
#
# The response holds the records under +key+, plus count (all matches, not just
# this page), page, per_page, next_page and previous_page. The last two are null
# when there is no such page.
module Paginated
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  private

  def render_page(scope, key:, &serialize)
    errors = {}
    page = whole_number_param(:page, 1, errors)
    per_page = whole_number_param(:per_page, DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, errors, max: MAX_PER_PAGE)
    return render_validation_failed(errors) if errors.any?

    count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
    # Past the end there is nothing to fetch. Skipping the query also keeps huge page numbers away from SQL.
    records = offset < count ? scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a : []

    render json: {
      key => records.map(&serialize),
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
  end

  # Reads a positive whole number from the query string. Anything else adds an
  # error for +name+ and returns nil.
  def whole_number_param(name, default, errors, max: nil)
    raw = params[name].to_s.strip
    return default if raw.empty?

    number = raw.to_i if raw.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
    return number if number&.positive? && (max.nil? || number <= max)

    errors[name] = [ max ? "must be a whole number from 1 to #{max}" : "must be a whole number of at least 1" ]
    nil
  end
end

# Reads a reply from a PATCH body. A reply can carry a comment, a status, or both.
module Replies
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  # The comment body to post. nil when the reply has no comment.
  def reply_body(input)
    input.key?(:comment) ? input.dig(:comment, :body).to_s : nil
  end

  # The status to set. nil leaves the status alone.
  def reply_status(input)
    input.key?(:status) ? input[:status].to_s : nil
  end

  # Renders 400 and returns true when the update names none of +keys+. The default keys are a comment and a status.
  def reject_empty_reply(input, keys: %i[comment status], message: "Send a comment, a status, or both.")
    return false if keys.any? { |key| input.key?(key) }

    render_error(:bad_request, "parameter_missing", message)
    true
  end
end

# Reads the filters on a list. Each filter is optional, and a blank value means no filter. A value that is not
# allowed adds an error under the parameter's name, so the caller can answer 422 instead of guessing.
module ListFilters
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # A user ID as the database stores it: digits only, within the bigint range.
  USER_ID_FORMAT = /\A\d{1,18}\z/

  private

  # One of +allowed+, or nil when the parameter is absent or blank.
  def choice_param(name, allowed, errors)
    value = params[name].to_s.strip
    return nil if value.empty?
    return value if allowed.include?(value)

    errors[name] = [ "must be one of #{allowed.join(", ")}" ]
    nil
  end

  # A user ID, or a word from +also+ returned as given, or nil when absent or blank.
  def user_id_param(name, errors, also: [])
    value = params[name].to_s.strip
    return nil if value.empty?
    return value if also.include?(value)
    return value.to_i if value.match?(USER_ID_FORMAT)

    errors[name] = [ "must be #{[ "a user ID", *also ].join(" or ")}" ]
    nil
  end

  # The search text exactly as typed, or nil when absent or blank. It is not trimmed, so the text the user types
  # is the text that is matched. Anything other than text is an error.
  def text_param(name, errors)
    value = params[name]
    return nil if value.blank?
    return value if value.is_a?(String) && !value.include?("\u0000")

    errors[name] = [ "must be text" ]
    nil
  end
end

# Offset pagination for list endpoints, using ?page= and ?per_page= (defaults 1 and 25).
#
# The response holds the records under +key+, plus count (all matches, not just
# this page), page, per_page, next_page and previous_page. The last two are null
# when there is no such page.
module Paginated
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  DEFAULT_PER_PAGE = 25
  MAX_PER_PAGE = 100

  private

  def render_page(scope, key:, &serialize)
    errors = {}
    page = whole_number_param(:page, 1, errors)
    per_page = whole_number_param(:per_page, DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, errors, max: MAX_PER_PAGE)
    return render_validation_failed(errors) if errors.any?

    count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page
    # Past the end there is nothing to fetch. Skipping the query also keeps huge page numbers away from SQL.
    records = offset < count ? scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).to_a : []

    render json: {
      key => records.map(&serialize),
      count: count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: page * per_page < count ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
  end

  # Reads a positive whole number from the query string. Anything else adds an
  # error for +name+ and returns nil.
  def whole_number_param(name, default, errors, max: nil)
    raw = params[name].to_s.strip
    return default if raw.empty?

    number = raw.to_i if raw.match?(/\A\d+\z/)
    return number if number&.positive? && (max.nil? || number <= max)

    errors[name] = [ max ? "must be a whole number from 1 to #{max}" : "must be a whole number of at least 1" ]
    nil
  end
end

# Reads a reply from a PATCH body. A reply can carry a comment, a status, or both.
module Replies
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  private

  # The comment body to post. nil when the reply has no comment.
  def reply_body(input)
    input.key?(:comment) ? input.dig(:comment, :body).to_s : nil
  end

  # The status to set. nil leaves the status alone.
  def reply_status(input)
    input.key?(:status) ? input[:status].to_s : nil
  end

  # Renders 400 and returns true when the update names none of +keys+. The default keys are a comment and a status.
  def reject_empty_reply(input, keys: %i[comment status], message: "Send a comment, a status, or both.")
    return false if keys.any? { |key| input.key?(key) }

    render_error(:bad_request, "parameter_missing", message)
    true
  end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# A customer's request for help and the conversation about it. Customers see it
# as a "request", staff as a "ticket". It is one record.
class Ticket < ApplicationRecord
  STATUSES = %w[open pending solved].freeze
  # Internal: how urgent staff consider the request. Every request starts normal.
  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  # Customers can only mark a request solved. Staff can choose any status.
  CUSTOMER_STATUSES = %w[solved].freeze
  # Default for an argument that was not sent. Unlike nil, which means "clear it" for the assignee.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true
  has_many :comments, -> { order(:created_at, :id) }, dependent: :delete_all, inverse_of: :ticket

  normalizes :subject, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }

  validates :subject, presence: true, length: { maximum: 255 }
  validates :status, inclusion: { in: STATUSES }
  validates :priority, inclusion: { in: PRIORITIES }
  validate :requester_belongs_to_account
  validate :assignee_must_be_active_staff, if: :will_save_change_to_assignee_id?

  # Most recently active first. The id breaks ties so pages never repeat or skip records.
  scope :recently_active, -> { order(updated_at: :desc, id: :desc) }
  scope :requested_by, ->(user) { where(requester: user) }
  scope :with_status, ->(status) { where(status: status) }
  scope :with_priority, ->(priority) { where(priority: priority) }
  scope :unassigned, -> { where(assignee_id: nil) }

  # Requests whose subject, or a public comment, contains +text+, ignoring case. The text is literal: % and _
  # and \ match only themselves. Private notes are not searched. A request is listed once, however many
  # comments match.
  scope :search, lambda { |text|
    pattern = "%#{sanitize_sql_like(text)}%"
    where(<<~SQL.squish, pattern: pattern)
      tickets.subject ILIKE :pattern
      OR EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 FROM comments
        WHERE comments.ticket_id = tickets.id AND comments.public AND comments.body ILIKE :pattern
      )
    SQL
  }

  # Opens a request from +requester+ with its first comment. Both are saved, or neither is.
  def self.open!(requester:, subject:, body:)
    ticket = new(account: requester.account, requester: requester, subject: subject, status: "open")
    ticket.reply!(author: requester, body: body, customer: true)
  end

  # Posts a reply, changes the status, the priority and/or the assignee, in one transaction.
  #
  # body:           the comment to post. nil posts nothing. Blank is an error.
  # status:         the status to set. nil keeps the current one.
  # customer:       customers may only mark the request solved. A customer reply reopens
  #                 a pending or solved request, unless it is solved in the same update.
  #                 A staff reply never changes the status by itself.
  # public_comment: false posts a private note, which only staff can see. Customers always post public comments.
  # assignee_id:    the staff member to assign, nil to clear, or UNCHANGED to leave it alone.
  # priority:       "normal" or "high". nil leaves it alone. Customers never set it.
  #
  # Only a status change or a public comment counts as activity and moves the request up the lists. Assigning,
  # changing the priority and private notes leave the request's timestamps alone.
  def reply!(author:, body: nil, status: nil, customer: false, public_comment: true, assignee_id: UNCHANGED,
             priority: nil)
    attributes = { author: author, body: body, status: status, customer: customer,
                   public_comment: public_comment, assignee_id: assignee_id, priority: priority }
    # Assigning checks that the person is still active. Suspension runs under the account lock, so the check
    # and the save must too, or a person suspended in between could end up assigned.
    return update_with_comment!(**attributes) if assignee_id.equal?(UNCHANGED)

    account.with_lock { update_with_comment!(**attributes) }
  end

  # What customers see: their own request, without the requester's details.
  def as_request_json
    {
      id: id,
      subject: subject,
      status: status,
      requester_id: requester_id,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

  # What staff see, including who opened the request, who is working on it and how urgent it is.
  def as_ticket_json

  PRIORITIES = %w[normal high].freeze
  # Customers can only mark a request solved. Staff can choose any status.
  CUSTOMER_STATUSES = %w[solved].freeze
  # Default for an argument that was not sent. Unlike nil, which means "clear it" for the assignee.
  UNCHANGED = Object.new.freeze

  belongs_to :requester, class_name: "User"
  belongs_to :assignee, class_name: "User", optional: true

# A business using the helpdesk. Everything else belongs to exactly one account.
class Account < ApplicationRecord
  # Cancelled accounts can be reactivated for this long, then purged for good.
  REACTIVATION_WINDOW = 90.days

  SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT = /\A[a-z0-9](?:[a-z0-9-]{0,61}[a-z0-9])\z/
  RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS = %w[admin api app assets mail smtp static status www].freeze

  # Declared before users, so requests and their comments go before the people who opened them.
  has_many :tickets, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :invitations, dependent: :destroy
  has_many :users, dependent: :destroy

  normalizes :name, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip }
  normalizes :subdomain, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :name, presence: true, length: { maximum: 120 }
  validates :subdomain,
            presence: true,
            uniqueness: true,
            format: { with: SUBDOMAIN_FORMAT, message: "may only use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens" },
            exclusion: { in: RESERVED_SUBDOMAINS, message: "is reserved" }

  scope :cancelled_before, ->(time) { where(cancelled_at: ..time) }

  def cancelled?
    cancelled_at.present?
  end

  def reactivation_deadline
    cancelled_at && (cancelled_at + REACTIVATION_WINDOW)
  end

  def reactivation_open?(now = Time.current)
    cancelled? && now < reactivation_deadline
  end

  # Cancelling stops ordinary access and signs every user out. The data is kept
  # until the reactivation window closes.
  def cancel!(now: Time.current)
    transaction do
      update!(cancelled_at: now)
      Session.where(user_id: users.select(:id)).delete_all
    end
  end

  def reactivate!
    update!(cancelled_at: nil)
  end

  # Permanently deletes accounts cancelled more than REACTIVATION_WINDOW ago,
  # along with all their users, sessions, tokens, requests and comments. Returns the number purged.
  def self.purge_cancelled!(now: Time.current)
    cutoff = now - REACTIVATION_WINDOW
    purged = 0

    cancelled_before(cutoff).ids.each do |id|
      transaction do
        # Re-check under a row lock: the account may have been reactivated since the query.
        account = lock.find_by(id: id)
        next unless account&.cancelled_at && account.cancelled_at <= cutoff

        account.destroy!
        purged += 1
      end
    end

    purged
  end

  def as_api_json
    {
      id: id,
      name: name,
      subdomain: subdomain,
      status: cancelled? ? "cancelled" : "active",
      cancelled_at: cancelled_at,
      reactivation_deadline: reactivation_deadline,
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end
end
"

# Emailed tokens (email verification, password reset). Each user has at most one
# live token of each kind. Issuing a new one replaces the old, and redeeming a
# token deletes it, so it works once.
module SingleUseToken
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, already used, or for another business.
  class InvalidToken < StandardError; end

  included do
    belongs_to :user

    validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  end

  class_methods do
    # Returns the raw token to email. Only its digest is stored.
    def issue!(user)
      raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
      user.with_lock do
        where(user_id: user.id).delete_all
        create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: self::TTL.from_now)
      end
      raw
    end

    # Deletes and returns the matching token record, or raises InvalidToken.
    # Call inside a transaction, so a later failure also gives the token back.
    def redeem!(raw, account: nil)
      scope = where(token_digest: digest(raw))
      scope = scope.where(user_id: account.users.select(:id)) if account

      record = scope.lock.first
      raise InvalidToken unless record&.expires_at&.future?

      record.destroy!
      record
    end

    def digest(raw)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
    end
  end
end

# token deletes it, so it works once.
module SingleUseToken
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, already used, or for another business.
  class InvalidToken < StandardError; end

  included do
    belongs_to :user

    validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  end

  class_methods do
    # Returns the raw token to email. Only its digest is stored.
    def issue!(user)
      raw = SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
      user.with_lock do
        where(user_id: user.id).delete_all
        create!(user: user, token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: self::TTL.from_now)
      end
      raw
    end

    # Deletes and returns the matching token record, or raises InvalidToken.
    # Call inside a transaction, so a later failure also gives the token back.
    def redeem!(raw, account: nil)
      scope = where(token_digest: digest(raw))
      scope = scope.where(user_id: account.users.select(:id)) if account

      record = scope.lock.first
      raise InvalidToken unless record&.expires_at&.future?

      record.destroy!
      record
    end

    def digest(raw)
      Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
    end
  end
end

# An emailed offer to join a business as an admin or agent. Customers register on their own, so they are never invited.
#
# Status comes from the timestamps, so expiry needs no job:
#   accepted  accepted_at is set
#   revoked   revoked_at is set, by an admin
#   pending   neither is set, and expires_at is in the future
#   expired   neither is set, and expires_at has passed
#
# An email can hold at most one pending invitation in a business, and cannot be invited when it already belongs
# to a user there. Issuing, resending, revoking and accepting all run under the account's row lock, as do customer
# registration and suspension, so two requests cannot both pass these checks.
class Invitation < ApplicationRecord
  TTL = 7.days
  ROLES = %w[admin agent].freeze
  STATUSES = %w[pending accepted revoked expired].freeze

  # Raised when a token is unknown, expired, revoked, accepted, or for another business.
  class InvalidInvitation < StandardError; end
  # Raised when an admin resends or revokes an invitation that was already accepted or revoked.
  class AlreadyClosed < StandardError; end

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :invited_by, class_name: "User", optional: true

  normalizes :email, with: ->(value) { value.to_s.strip.downcase }

  validates :email, presence: true, length: { maximum: 254 }, format: { with: URI::MailTo::EMAIL_REGEXP }
  validates :role, inclusion: { in: ROLES, message: "must be admin or agent" }
  validates :token_digest, :expires_at, presence: true
  # Only checked when an invitation is issued or resent, so existing records do not start failing later.
  validate :email_must_be_free, on: :issue

  # Invitations in one status. Accepted and revoked are final. Pending and expired depend on the clock.
  def self.with_status(status)
    now = Time.current
    unanswered = where(accepted_at: nil, revoked_at: nil)

    case status
    when "pending" then unanswered.where("expires_at > ?", now)
    when "expired" then unanswered.where("expires_at <= ?", now)
    when "accepted" then where.not(accepted_at: nil)
    when "revoked" then where(accepted_at: nil).where.not(revoked_at: nil)
    else raise ArgumentError, "unknown invitation status #{status.inspect}"
    end
  end

  # Returns [invitation, raw_token]. The raw token is only emailed, never stored or shown in the API.
  def self.issue!(account:, invited_by:, email:, role:)
    raw = generate_token
    invitation = nil
    account.with_lock do
      invitation = new(account: account, invited_by: invited_by, email: email, role: role,
                       token_digest: digest(raw), expires_at: TTL.from_now)
      invitation.save!(context: :issue)
    end
    [ invitation, raw ]
  end

  # the invitation must belong to it.
  def self.find_pending_by_token!(raw, account: nil, now: Time.current)
    raise InvalidInvitation if raw.blank?

    scope = where(token_digest: digest(raw))
    scope = scope.where(account: account) if account
    invitation = scope.includes(:account).first
    raise InvalidInvitation unless invitation&.status(now) == "pending"

    invitation
  end

  def self.digest(raw)
    Digest::SHA256.hexdigest(raw.to_s)
  end

  def self.generate_token
    SecureRandom.urlsafe_base64(32)
  end

  def status(now = Time.current)
    return "accepted" if accepted_at
    return "revoked" if revoked_at

    expires_at > now ? "pending" : "expired"
  end

  def open?
    accepted_at.nil? && revoked_at.nil?
  end

  # invitations. Returns the new raw token.
  def resend!
    raw = self.class.generate_token
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      raise AlreadyClosed unless open?

      self.token_digest = self.class.digest(raw)
      self.expires_at = TTL.from_now
      save!(context: :issue)
    end
    raw
  end

  def revoke!(now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      raise AlreadyClosed unless open?

      update!(revoked_at: now)
    end
  end

  # Creates the verified user with the invited email and role, and marks the invitation accepted. Both happen, or neither does.
  def accept!(name:, password:, now: Time.current)
    account.with_lock do
      reload
      raise InvalidInvitation unless status(now) == "pending"

      user = account.users.create!(name: name, email: email, password: password, role: role, verified_at: now)
      update!(accepted_at: now)
      user
    end
  end

    {
      id: id,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      status: status(now),
      expires_at: expires_at,
      accepted_at: accepted_at,
      revoked_at: revoked_at,
      invited_by: invited_by && { id: invited_by.id, name: invited_by.name },
      created_at: created_at,
      updated_at: updated_at
    }
  end

    return if email.blank? || account.nil?

    if account.users.exists?(email: email)
      errors.add(:email, "already belongs to a user in this business")
    end

    # A customer signs up for a business's portal, chosen by the X-Helpdesk-Account header.

    class RegistrationsController < ApplicationController
      def create
        account = account_from_header!
        return if performed?
        return render_error(:forbidden, "account_cancelled", "This business has been cancelled.") if account.cancelled?

        input = require_params(:user).permit(:name, :email, :password)

          user.valid?

          raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid, user if user.errors.any?

          user.save!
          verification_token = EmailVerification.issue!(user)
        end
        UserMailer.deliver_safely(:email_verification, user, verification_token)

        render json: { user: user.as_api_json }, status: :created
      end
    end
  end

module Api
  module V1
    class EmailVerificationsController < ApplicationController
      GENERIC_MESSAGE = "If that email belongs to an account that needs verifying, a verification link is on its way.".freeze

      # Sends a fresh verification link. Replaces any earlier link.
      def create
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        email = require_params(:email_verification).permit(:email)[:email]
        scope = (account ? account.users : User.all).where(email: email, verified_at: nil)

        scope.includes(:account).each do |user|
          token = EmailVerification.issue!(user)
          UserMailer.deliver_safely(:email_verification, user, token)
        end

        render json: { message: GENERIC_MESSAGE }, status: :accepted
      end

      def confirm
        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        token = require_params(:email_verification).permit(:token)[:token]
        user = nil

        EmailVerification.transaction do
          record = EmailVerification.redeem!(token, account: account)
          user = record.user
          user.verified_at ||= Time.current
          user.save!
        end

        render json: { message: "Email verified. You can sign in now.", user: user.as_api_json, account: user.account.as_api_json }

class ApplicationMailer < ActionMailer::Base
  # A proc, so HELPDESK_MAIL_FROM is read when mail is sent, not at boot.
  default from: proc { Helpdesk::Settings.mail_from }
  layout "mailer"
end
class UserMailer < ApplicationMailer
  # Sends a mail and logs failures instead of raising. A failed send must not
  # undo a committed signup or a freshly issued token; the user can ask for
  # another link.
  def self.deliver_safely(mail_name, *args)
    public_send(mail_name, *args).deliver_now
  rescue StandardError => e
    Rails.logger.error("[helpdesk] #{mail_name} email failed: #{e.class}: #{e.message}")
    nil
  end

  def email_verification(user, token)
    @user = user
    @account = user.account
    @link = Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_link("/verify-email", account: @account.subdomain, token: token)
    @valid_for = EmailVerification::TTL.inspect

    mail to: user.email, subject: "Verify your email for #{@account.name}"
  end

  # Invites someone to join the business as an admin or agent. The link opens the frontend's acceptance screen.
  def invitation(invitation, token)
    @invitation = invitation
    @account = invitation.account
    @role = invitation.role
    @link = Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_link("/accept-invitation", account: @account.subdomain, token: token)
    @valid_for = Invitation::TTL.inspect

    mail to: invitation.email, subject: "You're invited to join #{@account.name} on Helpdesk"
  end

  def password_reset(user, token)
    @user = user
    @account = user.account
    @link = Helpdesk::Settings.frontend_link("/reset-password", account: @account.subdomain, token: token)
    @valid_for = PasswordReset::TTL.inspect

    mail to: user.email, subject: "Reset your password for #{@account.name}"
  end
end

module Api
  module V1
    class SessionsController < ApplicationController
      before_action :authenticate_session!, only: :destroy

      available_while_cancelled :destroy

      # Sign in. With X-Helpdesk-Account, the email is looked up in that business.
      # Without it, the email must belong to exactly one business.
      def create
        credentials = require_params(:session).permit(:email, :password)
        password = credentials[:password].to_s

        account = optional_account_from_header
        return if performed?

        candidates = (account ? account.users : User.all).where(email: credentials[:email]).includes(:account).to_a
        matches = candidates.select { |user| user.authenticate(password) }

        if matches.empty?
          # Hash anyway when no user matched, so response time does not reveal whether the email exists.
          BCrypt::Password.create(password) if candidates.empty?
          return render_error(:unauthorized, "invalid_credentials", "Email or password is incorrect.")
        end

        if matches.many?
          return render_error(
            :unprocessable_entity,
            "account_required",
            "This email belongs to several businesses. Send the X-Helpdesk-Account header to choose one."
          )
        end

        user = matches.first
        return render_error(:forbidden, "user_suspended", "This user has been suspended. Ask an admin to reinstate it.") if user.suspended?
        return render_error(:forbidden, "email_not_verified", "Verify your email address before signing in.") unless user.verified?

        if user.account.cancelled? && !user.admin?
          return render_error(:forbidden, "account_cancelled", "This business has been cancelled.")
        end

        session, token = Session.issue!(user)
        render json: {
          session: { token: token, expires_at: session.expires_at },
          user: user.as_api_json,
          account: user.account.as_api_json
        }, status: :created
      end

      def destroy
        current_session.destroy!
        head :no_content
      end
    end
  end
end

# Shared helpers for the JSON API integration tests.
module ApiHelpers
  include ActiveSupport::Testing::TimeHelpers

  PASSWORD = "my-first-password".freeze
  NEW_PASSWORD = "my-new-password".freeze
  CUSTOMER_PASSWORD = "my-customer-password".freeze

  def api(method, path, body: nil, token: nil, account: nil, headers: {})
    request_headers = { "Accept" => "application/json" }.merge(headers)
    request_headers["Authorization"] = "Bearer #{token}" if token
    request_headers["X-Helpdesk-Account"] = account if account

    if body.nil?
      send(method, "/api/v1#{path}", headers: request_headers)
    else
      request_headers["CONTENT_TYPE"] = "application/json"
      send(method, "/api/v1#{path}", params: body.to_json, headers: request_headers)
    end
  end

  def api_get(path, **options) = api(:get, path, **options)
  def api_post(path, body = nil, **options) = api(:post, path, body: body, **options)
  def api_patch(path, body, **options) = api(:patch, path, body: body, **options)
  def api_put(path, body, **options) = api(:put, path, body: body, **options)
  def api_delete(path, **options) = api(:delete, path, **options)

  def json
    JSON.parse(response.body)
  end

  def signup!(subdomain: "acme", name: "Acme", email: "jo@acme.test", password: PASSWORD)
    api_post("/account/create", {
      account: {
        name: name,
        subdomain: subdomain,
        admin: { name: "Jo", email: email, password: password }
      }
    })
  end

  # Token from the newest mail sent to `to` whose link is for `account` and `path`.
  # Links carry the business, so two businesses sharing an email stay distinct.
  def link_token(to:, path:, account:)
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.reverse.find do |candidate|
      Array(candidate.to).include?(to) && candidate.body.decoded.include?("#{path}?account=#{account}&")
    end
    assert mail, "expected an email to #{to} linking to #{path} for #{account}"

    link = mail.body.decoded[%r{http://\S+}]
    Rack::Utils.parse_query(URI.parse(link).query).fetch("token")
  end

  def verification_token(email, account: "acme")
    link_token(to: email, path: "/verify-email", account: account)
  end

module ActionMailbox
  # The base class for all Action Mailbox ingress controllers.
  class BaseController < ActionController::Base
    skip_forgery_protection

    before_action :ensure_configured

    private
      def ensure_configured
        unless ActionMailbox.ingress == ingress_name
          head :not_found
        end
      end

      def ingress_name
        self.class.name.remove(/\AActionMailbox::Ingresses::/, /::InboundEmailsController\z/).underscore.to_sym
      end


      def authenticate_by_password
        if password.present?
          http_basic_authenticate_or_request_with name: "actionmailbox", password: password, realm: "Action Mailbox"
        else
          raise ArgumentError, "Missing required ingress credentials"
        end
      end

      def password
        Rails.application.credentials.dig(:action_mailbox, :ingress_password) || ENV["RAILS_INBOUND_EMAIL_PASSWORD"]
      end
  end
end

require "mail"

module ActionMailbox
  # The +InboundEmail+ is an Active Record that keeps a reference to the raw email stored in Active Storage
  # and tracks the status of processing. By default, incoming emails will go through the following lifecycle:
  #
  # * Pending: Just received by one of the ingress controllers and scheduled for routing.
  # * Processing: During active processing, while a specific mailbox is running its #process method.
  # * Delivered: Successfully processed by the specific mailbox.
  # * Failed: An exception was raised during the specific mailbox's execution of the +#process+ method.
  # * Bounced: Rejected processing by the specific mailbox and bounced to sender.
  #
  # Once the +InboundEmail+ has reached the status of being either +delivered+, +failed+, or +bounced+,
  # it'll count as having been +#processed?+. Once processed, the +InboundEmail+ will be scheduled for
  # automatic incineration at a later point.
  #
  # When working with an +InboundEmail+, you'll usually interact with the parsed version of the source,
  # which is available as a +Mail+ object from +#mail+. But you can also access the raw source directly
  # using the +#source+ method.
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  #   inbound_email.mail.from # => 'david@loudthinking.com'
  #   inbound_email.source # Returns the full rfc822 source of the email as text
  class InboundEmail < Record
    include Incineratable, MessageId, Routable

    has_one_attached :raw_email, service: ActionMailbox.storage_service
    enum :status, %i[ pending processing delivered failed bounced ]

    def mail
      @mail ||= Mail.from_source(source)
    end

    def source
      @source ||= raw_email.download
    end

    def processed?
      delivered? || failed? || bounced?
    end

    def instrumentation_payload # :nodoc:
      {
        id: id,
        message_id: message_id,
        status: status
      }
    end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

require "mail"

module ActionMailbox
  # The +InboundEmail+ is an Active Record that keeps a reference to the raw email stored in Active Storage
  # and tracks the status of processing. By default, incoming emails will go through the following lifecycle:
  #
  # * Pending: Just received by one of the ingress controllers and scheduled for routing.
  # * Processing: During active processing, while a specific mailbox is running its #process method.
  # * Delivered: Successfully processed by the specific mailbox.
  # * Failed: An exception was raised during the specific mailbox's execution of the +#process+ method.
  # * Bounced: Rejected processing by the specific mailbox and bounced to sender.
  #
  # Once the +InboundEmail+ has reached the status of being either +delivered+, +failed+, or +bounced+,
  # it'll count as having been +#processed?+. Once processed, the +InboundEmail+ will be scheduled for
  # automatic incineration at a later point.
  #
  # When working with an +InboundEmail+, you'll usually interact with the parsed version of the source,
  # which is available as a +Mail+ object from +#mail+. But you can also access the raw source directly
  # using the +#source+ method.
  #
  # Examples:
  #
  #   inbound_email.mail.from # => 'david@loudthinking.com'
  #   inbound_email.source # Returns the full rfc822 source of the email as text
  class InboundEmail < Record
    include Incineratable, MessageId, Routable

    has_one_attached :raw_email, service: ActionMailbox.storage_service
    enum :status, %i[ pending processing delivered failed bounced ]

    def mail
      @mail ||= Mail.from_source(source)
    end

    def source
      @source ||= raw_email.download
    end

    def processed?
      delivered? || failed? || bounced?
    end

    def instrumentation_payload # :nodoc:
      {
        id: id,
        message_id: message_id,
        status: status
      }
    end
  end
end

Two things in this code matter for the design:

1. `create_and_extract_message_id!` rescues `RecordNotUnique` and drops the message. Whether that dedupes depends on the unique index, which I'll check in the migration. If it covers `(message_id, checksum)` and not just a delivered row, a failed first delivery would block its retry. That's the "invalid deliveries must not block a later valid retry" requirement.
2. The relay ingress returns 204 even for duplicates, so dedupe happens silently in the database layer.

require "active_support/rescuable"

require "action_mailbox/callbacks"
require "action_mailbox/routing"

module ActionMailbox
  # = Action Mailbox \Base
  #
  # The base class for all application mailboxes. Not intended to be inherited from directly. Inherit from
  # +ApplicationMailbox+ instead, as that's where the app-specific routing is configured. This routing
  # is specified in the following ways:
  #
  #   class ApplicationMailbox < ActionMailbox::Base
  #     # Any of the recipients of the mail (whether to, cc, bcc) are matched against the regexp.
  #     routing /^replies@/i => :replies
  #
  #     # Any of the recipients of the mail (whether to, cc, bcc) needs to be an exact match for the string.
  #     routing "help@example.com" => :help
  #
  #     # Any callable (proc, lambda, etc) object is passed the inbound_email record and is a match if true.
  #     routing ->(inbound_email) { inbound_email.mail.to.size > 2 } => :multiple_recipients
  #
  #     # Any object responding to #match? is called with the inbound_email record as an argument. Match if true.
  #     routing CustomAddress.new => :custom
  #
  #     # Any inbound_email that has not been already matched will be sent to the BackstopMailbox.
  #     routing :all => :backstop
  #   end
  #
  # Application mailboxes need to override the #process method, which is invoked by the framework after
  # callbacks have been run. The callbacks available are: +before_processing+, +after_processing+, and
  # +around_processing+. The primary use case is to ensure that certain preconditions to processing are fulfilled
  # using +before_processing+ callbacks.
  #
  # If a precondition fails to be met, you can halt the processing using the +#bounced!+ method,
  # which will silently prevent any further processing, but not actually send out any bounce notice. You
  # can also pair this behavior with the invocation of an Action Mailer class responsible for sending out
  # an actual bounce email. This is done using the #bounce_with method, which takes the mail object returned
  # by an Action Mailer method, like so:
  #
  #   class ForwardsMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  #     before_processing :ensure_sender_is_a_user
  #
  #     private
  #       def ensure_sender_is_a_user
  #         unless User.exists?(email_address: mail.from)
  #           bounce_with UserRequiredMailer.missing(inbound_email)
  #         end
  #       end
  #   end
  #
  # During the processing of the inbound email, the status will be tracked. Before processing begins,
  # the email will normally have the +pending+ status. Once processing begins, just before callbacks
  # and the #process method is called, the status is changed to +processing+. If processing is allowed to
  # complete, the status is changed to +delivered+. If a bounce is triggered, then +bounced+. If an unhandled
  # exception is bubbled up, then +failed+.
  #
  # Exceptions can be handled at the class level using the familiar
  # ActiveSupport::Rescuable approach:
  #
  #   class ForwardsMailbox < ApplicationMailbox
  #     rescue_from(ApplicationSpecificVerificationError) { bounced! }
  #   end
  class Base
    include ActiveSupport::Rescuable
    include ActionMailbox::Callbacks, ActionMailbox::Routing

    attr_reader :inbound_email
    delegate :mail, :delivered!, :bounced!, to: :inbound_email

    delegate :logger, to: ActionMailbox

    def self.receive(inbound_email)
      new(inbound_email).perform_processing
    end

    def initialize(inbound_email)
      @inbound_email = inbound_email
    end

    def perform_processing # :nodoc:
      ActiveSupport::Notifications.instrument "process.action_mailbox", instrumentation_payload do
        track_status_of_inbound_email do
          run_callbacks :process do
            process
          end
        end
      rescue => exception
        # TODO: Include a reference to the inbound_email in the exception raised so error handling becomes easier
        rescue_with_handler(exception) || raise
      end
    end

    def process
      # Override in subclasses
    end

    def finished_processing? # :nodoc:
      inbound_email.delivered? || inbound_email.bounced?
    end

    # Enqueues the given +message+ for delivery and changes the inbound email's status to +:bounced+.
    def bounce_with(message)
      inbound_email.bounced!
      message.deliver_later
    end

    # Immediately sends the given +message+ and changes the inbound email's status to +:bounced+.
    def bounce_now_with(message)
      inbound_email.bounced!
      message.deliver_now
    end

    private
      def instrumentation_payload
        {
          mailbox: self,
          inbound_email: inbound_email.instrumentation_payload
        }
      end

      def track_status_of_inbound_email
        inbound_email.processing!
        yield
        inbound_email.delivered! unless inbound_email.bounced?
      rescue
        inbound_email.failed!
        raise
      end
  end
end

module ActionMailbox
  # Encapsulates a route, which can then be matched against an inbound_email and provide a lookup of the matching
  # mailbox class. See examples for the different route addresses and how to use them in the ActionMailbox::Base
  # documentation.
  class Router::Route
    attr_reader :address, :mailbox_name

    def initialize(address, to:)
      @address, @mailbox_name = address, to

      ensure_valid_address
    end

    def match?(inbound_email)
      case address
      when :all
        true
      when String
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.casecmp?(recipient) }
      when Regexp
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.match?(recipient) }
      when Proc
        address.call(inbound_email)
      else
        address.match?(inbound_email)
      end
    end

    def mailbox_class
      "#{mailbox_name.to_s.camelize}Mailbox".constantize
    end

    private
      def ensure_valid_address
        unless [ Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc ].any? { |klass| address.is_a?(klass) } || address.respond_to?(:match?)
          raise ArgumentError, "Expected a Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc, or matchable, got #{address.inspect}"
        end
      end
  end
end

# frozen_string_literal: true

module ActionMailbox
  # Routing a new InboundEmail is an asynchronous operation, which allows the ingress controllers to quickly
  # accept new incoming emails without being burdened to hang while they're actually being processed.
  class RoutingJob < ActiveJob::Base

module ActionMailbox
  # Encapsulates a route, which can then be matched against an inbound_email and provide a lookup of the matching
  # mailbox class. See examples for the different route addresses and how to use them in the ActionMailbox::Base
  # documentation.
  class Router::Route
    attr_reader :address, :mailbox_name

    def initialize(address, to:)
      @address, @mailbox_name = address, to

      ensure_valid_address
    end

    def match?(inbound_email)
      case address
      when :all
        true
      when String
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.casecmp?(recipient) }
      when Regexp
        inbound_email.mail.recipients.any? { |recipient| address.match?(recipient) }
      when Proc
        address.call(inbound_email)
      else
        address.match?(inbound_email)
      end
    end

    def mailbox_class
      "#{mailbox_name.to_s.camelize}Mailbox".constantize
    end

    private
      def ensure_valid_address
        unless [ Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc ].any? { |klass| address.is_a?(klass) } || address.respond_to?(:match?)
          raise ArgumentError, "Expected a Symbol, String, Regexp, Proc, or matchable, got #{address.inspect}"
        end
      end
  end

messages.content:
The generator placed both migrations after the last existing one. Next are my own migrations, which cover three things:
1. **Action Mailbox uniqueness.** Its default unique index on `(message_id, message_checksum)` would reject a retry of a failed or rejected delivery. I'll replace it with a plain index. Dedupe will move to the point where a message actually creates a comment.
2. **Tickets.** An `origin` column (`portal` or `email`) and a per-ticket `reply_key` for the private reply address, backfilled for existing rows.
3. **Comments.** An `inbound_message_id` with a partial unique index. It's the durable dedupe key and only gets written when a message really creates something.

arguments.command:
cd /app && head -3 db/migrate/20261126000005_create_active_storage_tables.active_storage.rb && cat > db/migrate/20261126000007_relax_action_mailbox_message_uniqueness.rb <<'EOF'
# Action Mailbox refuses any delivery whose Message-ID and bytes match an earlier one, even when that earlier
# delivery failed or was rejected. A retry of an invalid delivery must still be processed, so duplicates are
# caught where they matter: a message that becomes a ticket or comment records its Message-ID there
# (comments.inbound_message_id). Action Mailbox's own rows only keep the record of each delivery.
class RelaxActionMailboxMessageUniqueness < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.1]
  def up
    remove_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, name: "index_action_mailbox_inbound_emails_uniqueness"
    add_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, :message_id
  end

  def down
    remove_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, :message_id
    add_index :action_mailbox_inbound_emails, %i[message_id message_checksum],
              name: "index_action_mailbox_inbound_emails_uniqueness", unique: true
  end
end
EOF
cat > db/migrate/20261126000008_add_origin_and_reply_key_to_tickets.rb <<'EOF'
# origin says how a request arrived: through the portal, or by email to the business's support address.
# reply_key names the ticket's private reply address (<subdomain>+<reply_key>@<support domain>).
class AddOriginAndReplyKeyToTickets < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.1]
  def up
    add_column :tickets, :origin, :string, null: false, default: "portal"
    add_column :tickets, :reply_key, :string

    # Existing tickets get a random key too, so every ticket has a private reply address.
    execute "UPDATE tickets SET reply_key = md5(random()::text || clock_timestamp()::text || id::text)"
    change_column_null :tickets, :reply_key, false
    add_index :tickets, :reply_key, unique: true
  end

  def down
    remove_index :tickets, :reply_key
    remove_column :tickets, :reply_key
    remove_column :tickets, :origin
  end
end
EOF
cat > db/migrate/20261126000009_add_inbound_message_id_to_comments.rb <<'EOF'
# The Message-ID of the email that created this comment. Only a message that was accepted records one, so a
# message that was rejected leaves no trace and can be retried. The unique index makes a repeated delivery
# of an accepted message a no-op.
class AddInboundMessageIdToComments < ActiveRecord::Migration[8.1]
  def change
    add_column :comments, :inbound_message_id, :string
    add_index :comments, :inbound_message_id, unique: true, where: "inbound_message_id IS NOT NULL",
              name: "index_comments_on_inbound_message_id"
  end
end
EOF
